extracted.intended_audience: Applicants (individuals, teams, organizations) seeking ARPA-E OPEN 2021 financial assistance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal requirements for preparing and submitting Concept Papers, Full Applications, and Replies to Reviewer Comments for the ARPA-E OPEN 2021 Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA DE-FOA-0002459). Covers eligibility, content/format, submission systems, intellectual property, cost share, and evaluation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept Paper length and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Concept Paper must not exceed 4 pages in length and must include the following: Concept Summary; Innovation and Impact; Proposed Work; Team Organization and Capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit Concept Paper in Adobe PDF format by the stated deadline. See Section IV.C for further content and form guidance. Concept Papers are mandatory (Required Documents Checklist). Applicants are encouraged to submit at least 48 hours in advance of the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Technical Subcategory(ies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Concept Paper and Full Application must identify a Technical Subcategory or Subcategories for the proposed technology from the list provided in the FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may select a single Technical Subcategory or multiple subcategories (from same or different Technical Categories). If the proposed technology does not fall within any listed subcategory, select Category 7, Subcategory L: 'Other Energy Technologies Not Listed Above.' This identification is used to organize submissions for merit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of potential impact on ARPA-E Mission Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must address the potential impact of the proposed technology on ARPA-E’s Mission Areas: (i) reductions of imports of energy from foreign sources; (ii) reductions of energy-related emissions, including greenhouse gases; and (iii) improvement in the energy efficiency of all economic sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In an OPEN FOA the burden of demonstrating potential impact lies solely upon the applicant. The critical question applicants should consider is: 'If it works, will it matter?' Make the strongest possible case why the proposed technology will matter and how it advances one or more Mission Areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformational and disruptive potential
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-E funds high-risk, potentially transformational research that can create fundamentally new learning curves and potentially be disruptive in the marketplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should explain how the technology could generate a new learning curve (significantly better cost/performance vs incumbents) and provide evidence of disruptive potential, e.g., capability for manufacturing at competitive cost and deployment at scale. ARPA-E recognizes many projects will fail; emphasis is on high-impact potential if successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on applied research and experimental development
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-E funds applied research and experimental development (not basic research). Applied research is directed toward a specific practical aim; experimental development is creative, systematic work directed at producing new products or processes or improving existing ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking support for basic research should contact DOE’s Office of Science. Clearly describe how the project falls within applied research/experimental development and the pathway to technical milestones/deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and period of performance limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual awards may vary between $250,000 and $10 million in Federal share. The period of performance for funding agreements may not exceed 36 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA-E expects to make approximately $100 million available and anticipates making ~30–50 awards. Propose budgets and timelines consistent with these constraints and justify requested Federal share in accordance with cost share rules (Section III.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible Applicants include Individuals, Domestic Entities, Foreign Entities, and Consortium Entities as described in Section III.A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Section III.A for detailed eligibility rules and any special rules for FFRDCs, GOCOs, GOGOs. Confirm applicant type and ensure required forms and documentation reflect entity type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost share requirements and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Sharing is required under this FOA as described in Section III.B: Base Cost Share Requirement; Increased Cost Share Requirement; Reduced Cost Share Requirement; Cost Share Allocation; Cost Share Types and Allowability; Cost Share Contributions by FFRDCs and GOGOs; Cost Share Verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the FOA’s cost share rules precisely, document sources of non-Federal contributions, ensure allowability under 2 C.F.R. Part 200, and be prepared for verification. Some categories (e.g., class patent waiver eligibility) reference specific cost-share thresholds (e.g., large business/foreign entities may need ≥20% cost share to elect title).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliant and responsiveness criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must meet detailed compliance and responsiveness criteria (see Sections III.C.1 through III.C.4) to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are responsible for meeting each submission requirement and compliance criterion; failure to comply may result in rejection. See Section III.C for specifics on formatting, required forms, and responsiveness to FOA instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on number of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limits on the number of submissions an entity or investigator may make under this FOA (see Section III for limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Section III (Limitation on Number of Submissions) to confirm whether multiple concept papers, full applications, or team roles are restricted and ensure compliance with any caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and use of ARPA-E eXCHANGE
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply to this FOA, Applicants must register with and submit application materials through ARPA-E eXCHANGE (https://arpa-e-foa.energy.gov/Registration.aspx).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For detailed guidance on using ARPA-E eXCHANGE, see Section IV.H.1. Problems with eXCHANGE should be sent to ExchangeHelp@hq.doe.gov. Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit at least 48 hours before the deadline to avoid portal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Concept Papers and other submission components must be submitted by stated deadlines in required formats (e.g., Concept Paper as Adobe PDF by the deadline). Applicants are responsible for meeting each submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are strict; ARPA-E encourages early submission (at least 48 hours before deadline). Submission components and deadlines are listed in the Required Documents Checklist and Section IV.A–IV.E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full and complete disclosure requirement (Business Assurances & Disclosures Form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are required to make a full and complete disclosure of the information requested in the Business Assurances & Disclosures Form. Disclosure of the requested information is mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to make a full and complete disclosure may result in rejection of submissions, termination of negotiations, modification/suspension/termination of awards, debarment proceedings, or civil/criminal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-E expects to retain copies of all Concept Papers, Full Applications, Replies to Reviewer Comments, and other submissions. No submissions will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By applying, Applicants consent to ARPA-E’s retention of their submissions. Do not expect returned materials; mark confidential material appropriately per marking rules (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking of confidential, proprietary, or privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions containing confidential, proprietary, or privileged information should be marked: include a cover sheet notice of restriction; identify specific pages containing confidential information; header/footer marking on each page containing such material; and mark each line/paragraph with double brackets or highlighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required cover sheet language: 'Notice of Restriction on Disclosure and Use of Data: Pages [___] of this document may contain confidential, proprietary, or privileged information...'. Failure to comply with marking requirements may result in disclosure under FOIA or other use/disclosure by the Government. The Government may use/disclose any information not appropriately marked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including Protected Personally Identifiable Information (Protected PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may not include any Protected Personally Identifiable Information (Protected PII) in their submissions to ARPA-E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of Protected PII prohibited in submissions include Social Security Numbers; place or date of birth associated with an individual; mother’s maiden name; biometric records (fingerprint, iris scan, DNA); medical history or conditions; metric information (weight, height, blood pressure); criminal history; financial information (credit card numbers, bank account numbers); performance appraisals tied to individuals; security clearance history (except actual clearances held).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property: title to subject inventions and Bayh-Dole rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership of subject inventions is governed by statute. Typically, domestic small businesses, educational institutions, and nonprofits may elect to retain title under the Bayh-Dole Act (35 U.S.C. § 200 et seq.), subject to timely patent filing and other obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other parties (e.g., large businesses, foreign entities) are governed by 42 U.S.C. § 5908 unless a class patent waiver applies. Class waivers may permit large businesses and foreign entities meeting certain requirements (such as ≥20% cost share) to elect to retain title. If title is retained, timely patent filing is required; waiver requests follow 10 C.F.R. § 784 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government rights: government use license and march-in rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Government retains a nonexclusive, nontransferable, irrevocable, paid-up license to practice or have practiced any subject invention worldwide. The Government also retains 'march-in rights' allowing it to require licenses under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: March-in rights may be exercised if: the owner/licensee has not taken effective steps to achieve practical application within a reasonable time; has not alleviated health/safety needs; has not met public use requirements under Federal statutes; or the U.S. Manufacturing requirement has not been met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights in technical data (background vs generated data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical data rights differ based on whether data was developed solely at private expense before the award (background or 'Limited Rights Data') or generated under the award (Generated Data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background data generally will not be required to be delivered except as necessary for monitoring/evaluation. The Government normally retains broad rights to technical data produced under ARPA-E awards, including public distribution, though certain categories of generated data may be protected from public disclosure for up to five years (specific award provisions will set details). Invention disclosures may be protected for a reasonable time to allow patent filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOA postings and modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: FOAs and any modifications are posted on ARPA-E eXCHANGE, Grants.gov, and FedConnect. Modifications to the FOA are posted to these websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register with FedConnect/ARPA-E eXCHANGE as an interested party to receive email notifications upon FOA modifications. It is recommended to register promptly after FOA release to receive timely notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication rules and the 'quiet period'
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon issuance of the FOA, only the Contracting Officer may communicate with Applicants. ARPA-E personnel and support contractors are prohibited from communicating with Applicants regarding the FOA until ARPA-E’s public announcement of selections ('quiet period').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the quiet period, submit all FOA questions to ARPA-E-CO@hq.doe.gov. ARPA-E will post responses weekly to the FOA-specific FAQ. ARPA-E will cease accepting questions approximately 10 business days in advance of each submission deadline. For eXCHANGE technical issues, contact ExchangeHelp@hq.doe.gov. ARPA-E will not accept or respond to communications by other means (fax, phone, mail, hand delivery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Debriefings and reviewer comments process
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-E does not provide debriefings. Applicants will receive notifications encouraging/discouraging submission of Full Applications based on Concept Paper assessments and will receive reviewer comments on Full Applications before the submission deadline for Replies to Reviewer Comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA-E provides an opportunity to submit Replies to Reviewer Comments (see Section IV.E). The selection process may include pre-selection clarifications, down-selects, and selection for award negotiations (see Section IV.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking consequences and FOIA risk
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government may use or disclose any information that is not appropriately marked or otherwise restricted, regardless of source; the Government is not liable for disclosure or use of unmarked information and may use/disclose it for any purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the FOA's marking instructions precisely (cover sheet language, page identification, header/footer, double brackets/highlighting) to preserve confidentiality where appropriate. Improper marking risks public disclosure under FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance audit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Prime Recipient organized as a for-profit entity expending $750,000 or more of DOE funds in the entity’s fiscal year (including funds expended as a Subrecipient) must have an annual compliance audit performed. Similar thresholds apply to educational institutions, nonprofits, or state/local governments as Prime Recipients or Subrecipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Subpart F of 2 C.F.R. Part 200 and 2 C.F.R. Part 910 for audit rules and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestones and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: A Milestone is a tangible, observable measurement provided upon successful completion of a project task or sub-task. A Deliverable is the quantifiable goods or services provided upon successful completion of a project task or sub-task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should define clear, measurable milestones and deliverables that connect tasks/subtasks to overall objectives. These will be used to monitor progress and for award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and non-return of submissions consent
rubrics_metrics.description: By applying to ARPA-E for funding, Applicants consent to ARPA-E’s retention of their submissions; submissions will not be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send originals expecting return. Keep local copies and ensure confidential information is marked as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and evaluation organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be organized for merit review according to Technical Categories/Subcategories; evaluation criteria exist for Concept Papers, Full Applications, and Replies to Reviewer Comments (see Section V).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the proposal is placed into the correct technical category and that content addresses the specific evaluation criteria (e.g., impact, innovation, team capability, feasibility). Consult Section V for details on review criteria and Section IV for content guidance for each submission stage.
